policy_name: FY2024 NDAA, Section 350 ("Strategy and assessment on use of automation and artificial intelligence for shipyard optimization")
question: What specific reporting requirements and deadlines are established to ensure accountability for the development and implementation of the AI strategy and assessment outlined in Section 350?
answer_low_temp:
1. The strategy for leveraging AI for shipyard optimization, as outlined in Section 350(a), requires the Secretary of the Navy to develop and implement the strategy in coordination with the Shipyard Infrastructure Optimization Program of the Department of the Navy. There are no specific reporting requirements or deadlines mentioned for this strategy.

2. The assessment of costs and potential savings of adopting AI predictive maintenance technologies, as outlined in Section 350(b), requires the Secretary of the Navy to conduct the assessment and include the following:
   - An analysis of maintenance delays and costs due to unplanned and unpredicted maintenance issues (Section 350(b)(1)).
   - An evaluation of opportunities to demonstrate commercial best practices at shipyards, including the demonstration of AI technologies (Section 350(b)(2)).
   - An identification of shipyard assets with sufficient data available for near-term demonstrations of AI predictive maintenance technologies and an estimate of resources needed to accelerate such demonstrations (Section 350(b)(3)).

3. The Secretary of the Navy is required to provide a briefing to the congressional defense committees not later than 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act, as outlined in Section 350(c). The briefing should include:
   - The strategy under Section 350(a) (Section 350(c)(1)).
   - The results of the assessment under Section 350(b) (Section 350(c)(2)).
   - A plan to execute any measures pursuant to such assessment (Section 350(c)(3)).

Citations:
- National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021, Section 350 (https://www.congress.gov/bill/116th-congress/house-bill/6395/text)
answer_high_temp: 180 days after the date of enactment, the Secretary of the Navy is required to provide a briefing to the congressional defense committees on the strategy under Section 350(a), the results of the assessment under Section 350(b), and a plan to execute any measures pursuant to such assessment (Section 350(c)).
